items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: But McShann's band, when we worked out that morning on the Plaza, we played things like... I think when we finally got Bird, he may have goofed a little hit.

ctx.x: Almost the earliest thing I can remember is sort of banjo players who played faster, you know, and drown everybody else out.

Yeah, exciting as it can be. And in those days -- for a guy were playing a lead instrument, and he could play "The Flight of the Bumblebee", he was the greatest. He was like Charlie Parker is today, you know. They'd say, man, that guy's playing "The Flight of the Bumblebee" on this saxophone, or on this trumpet. the and maybe playing all the wrong notes and everything, but he's exciting, you know.

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: It wasn't that same way it was doing to Jackknife, scratching his chin, you know, scratching his face, which is always an obvious sign, you know.

ctx.x: How -- how much was Bird's sort of addiction showing in these McCann years. Was it --

Well, it wasn't that same way it was doing to Jackknife, scratching his chin, you know, scratching his face, which is always an obvious sign, you know. It wasn't that. In fact, it's very rarely you would see him doing the way, he was standing there nodding and that sort of thing.
But you could tell. And -- I mean was he -- did he generally remain sort of in good control or not?
